purpose:

to Vivid Resourcing for the provision of a temporary Housing
Options Triage Officer.
content:
Approval of an exemption from
Contract Standing Orders to enable the direct award of a contract
to Vivid Resourcing for the provision of a temporary Housing
Options Triage Officer.
 

The Homelessness Service
requires temporary capacity to support operational service
delivery.
 
Candidates provided through the
existing agency framework were interviewed but were not considered
suitable for the role.
 
The service has identified a
specific candidate who is available and suitable to undertake the
assignment. The proposed appointment is through Vivid Resourcing,
which is not a framework supplier.
 
The exemption will allow the
Council to secure the required temporary resource without delay and
maintain service delivery within the Homelessness
Service.

Option 1 - Approve the
exemption and direct award to Vivid
Resourcing
This option enables the service to secure the identified candidate
and maintain operational capacity within the Housing Options
service. This is the recommended option.
 
Option 2 - Undertake a
competitive quotation process
This option would delay the appointment and may not result in the
Council being able to secure the identified candidate. Framework
agencies have already been approached, and suitable candidates were
not identified.

content:
To agree the Stratford-on-Avon District
Council Community/Warm Hub Grant Support Scheme 2026 grant scheme
design, guidance notes and application process.

Following the report 
here approved by the Cabinet on 6 July 2026 a budget of
£25,000 be established from the Business Rates Equalisation
Reserve, which warm hubs can apply to for funding to maintain and
enhance their provision. We plan to distribute financial support to
qualifying applicant organisations to enable them to achieve our
aim of:
 
Support, prolong and enhance community
wellbeing activity through community/warm hub events bringing
together members of the whole community but with a focus on more
vulnerable residents.
 
We are looking to support community/warm hubs
meeting the below objectives:
 

Improving the sustainability of
community/warm hubs through providing funding for venue hire or
similar;
Improving experience through
enhancing activities held at the community/warm hub;
Improving the administration of the
community/warm hub through funding administrative costs, including
insurance, compliance costs, DBS checks, energy bills, or similar;
and
Provision of funding to cover other
costs associated with the development and delivery of
community/warm hubs.

 
To deliver these grants we have developed a
grant scheme design, accompanying this paper, describing the
following aspects of the scheme:
 

What type of applications are we
looking for
How much money can your organisation
ask for
Time frames
Monitoring, Reporting &
Evaluation
Governance
Who cannot apply for the funding and
what will not be funded
Help and advice on running safe
events
Checklist of Eligibility
Application and assessment process,
and
Template application form

 
The next stage will be to launch the grant at
the beginning of September including launch events in person and on
TEAMs and establishment of a micro-site on the district
council’s website.
The Leader is happy to support this.

Significant discussion took place both before
and during the Cabinet meeting on the 6 July and the necessity of a
swift response to ensure that Warm/Community Hubs have access to
funding before the onset of winter was considered to justify a
grant scheme delivered by the team, rather than a third party, as
this is likely to be more quickly deployed.
topline: The Stratford-on-Avon District Council has decided to approve a grant support scheme for community/warm hubs to enhance community wellbeing activities and support vulnerable residents.

decision_maker: Head of Housing, Revenues and Customer Services
content:
That Stratford-on-Avon District
Council extend the Community Builder project delivered by WCAVA for
a further 12 months in line with the contract
specification.
 

The Community Builder project
was developed through the Social Inclusion Partnership to support
stronger, more resilient communities in Bishopton and Clopton. The
initial pilot focused on two areas identified as experiencing
higher levels of need and was designed to help residents, community
organisations and local partners build on existing assets,
strengthen local connections and create activity shaped by
community priorities.
 
The project has continued to
operate through an Asset Based Community Development approach,
recognising that residents and community organisations have skills,
knowledge and relationships that can be supported and developed.
The Community Builder role provides dedicated capacity to listen,
connect, broker relationships, support practical delivery and help
local ideas become sustainable community action.
 
The project is co-funded by
Stratford-on-Avon District Council (£27,000 per year),
Stratford Town Trust (£23,000 per year) and
Stratford-upon-Avon Town Council (£5,000 per year). The
contract is five years in total structured in a 2+1+1+1 format. It
is at the end of the first 2 years with the option to extend for a
further year subject to funding and meeting its KPI’s.
Stratford-on-Avon District Council, Stratford Town Trust and
Stratford-upon-Avon Town Council have confirmed funding for the
12-month extension.
 
Based on the combined KPI data,
stakeholder feedback, Bishopton survey findings and June 2026
review of the contract, the Community Builder role is performing
strongly against the contractual expectations and remains highly
relevant to resident priorities. The Project Board including
funders Stratford-on-Avon District Council, Stratford Town Trust
and Stratford-upon-Avon Town Council are supportive of the
extension.

Grant 2026
content:
Approval for Grant Scheme
Design - Stratford-on-Avon District Council Healthy and Sustainable
Food For All - Community Food Projects
Grant 2026
 

To agree the Stratford-on-Avon
District Council Healthy and Sustainable Food For All - Community Food Projects Grant 2026 grant
scheme design, guidance notes and application process.
 

Following a Notice of Motion
(here)
that was approved by the Cabinet on 7 October 2024 a growth bid
(see attached) was developed by Cllr Petrovic and Cllr Hatch for
the 2026/27 year to fund work to support rural producers and tackle
food insecurity in Stratford District. The growth bid was partially
successful, and the project was awarded £50,000.
 
Following detailed discussions
with Tony Perks and Ali Chafekar it was agreed that the Communities
and Social Inclusion Team would lead on the food insecurity element
of the project and work with local stakeholders and the voluntary,
community, faith and social enterprise sector (VCFSE) to develop a
grant scheme for approval.
 
Several meetings have taken
place including a Listening Event attended by 25+ stakeholders and
potential VCFSE applicant organisation to shape the
grant. 
 
The work with key members and
the Listening Event has enabled the development of a grant offer
likely to be both popular and proportionate. Attached to this
document is a guidance note & application form for use by
potential applicants for the Healthy and Sustainable Food For All -
Community Food Projects Grant 2026. The note details the
following:
 
1)  
Scheme aims and objectives
2)  
Grant types available
·      
Small Project Grant
·      
Large Project Grant
·      
Innovation Grant
3)  
Levels of funding available
4)  
Timeframes
5)  
Monitoring and reporting requirements
6)  
Governance
7)  
Food hygiene requirements and advice
8)  
Application process and application form.
 
The next stage will be to
launch the grant over the next four weeks including launch events
in person and on TEAMs and establishment of a micro-site on the
district council’s website.
 

A variety of options were
considered as part of the scheme design process.  Many of these have been woven into the scheme and
some have been discounted, in particular
the more grower support element of the original growth bid
which is been taken forward by the Economic Development
Team.
topline: The Head of Housing, Revenues and Customer Services has decided to approve the Stratford-on-Avon District Council Healthy and Sustainable Food For All - Community Food Projects Grant 2026 scheme design and application process.

content:
Councillor Coles – Housing and Customer Services
Portfolio
 
Consideration was given to the
Warwickshire Joint Local Health and Wellbeing Strategy 2026-31
which set out how the Warwickshire’s Health and Wellbeing
Board partners would work together to support improvements in local
health and wellbeing outcomes, prevent ill health, and reduce
inequalities in health outcomes.
 
In receiving the report, it was
noted that tree county wide priorities had been
identified:
 

1.  
Creating the conditions to support good mental
health and wellbeing, prioritising children and young people,
enabling them to flourish;
 

2.  
Tackling the factors that cause poverty and lead to
inequalities in health and wellbeing; and
 

3.  
Supporting people to move more and eat
well.
 
A set of high-level actions to
support the priorities had been established, informed by three
Place Partnerships, each with its own tailored focus.
 
It was further noted that the
next step would be to prepare several local place-based delivery
plans, including one to cover South Warwickshire.
 
The options available to The
Cabinet were to note, amend and then note or not to note the
Warwickshire Joint Local Health and Wellbeing Strategy
2026-31.
 
Accordingly, it was
 
         
RESOLVED:
 
(1)        
That the contents of the Warwickshire Joint Local
Health and Wellbeing Strategy 2026-31 be noted;

 
(2)        
That Stratford-on-Avon District Council’s
officers continue to engage with the process of the development of
a local place-based delivery plan for South Warwickshire, ensuring
that this aligned with the Stratford-on-Avon District Council
Growing Opportunities Plan; and
 
(3)        
That Stratford-on-Avon District Council’s
officers continue their participatory role in the South
Warwickshire Place Partnership, in order
to steer delivery of the emerging local place-based delivery

Councillor Coles – Housing and Customer Services
Portfolio
 
Consideration was given to a
response to a Notice of Motion presented to Council on 20 April
2026 regarding Funding for Warm Hubs.
 
The Motion called for the
Council to address the challenges resultant from the closure of
Warwickshire Rural Community Council (WRCC) and earmark a reserve
of £50,000 in 2026/27 to support a properly constituted
Community Interest Company or Charity that would take over the
function relating to Warm Hubs across the District. The Motion also
called for the Council to write to other District and Borough
Leaders in Warwickshire requesting that they provide similar
support to Warm Hubs in their District or Borough.
 
In receiving the report, The
Cabinet noted that it provided a summary of the work undertaken to
establish the impact of the closure of WRCC and highlighted a range
of options that went some way to backfilling the gaps left by its
closure.
 
On the invitation of the Chair,
the following speakers addressed the meeting:
 

·      
Councillor Shenton – Proposer of
Motion

·      
Councillor Fleming – Seconder of
Motion
 
The Head of Housing, Revenues
and Customer Services agreed that engagement with the proposer and
seconder of the Motion had not been carried out, and it was
suggested that it could be added to the recommendations to
Council.
 
The options available to The
Cabinet were to approve the recommendations, request the
development of alternative recommendations or not approve the
recommendations.
 
Following which, it
was
 
        
RECOMMENDED to Council:
 
(1)      
That the importance of the role WRCC undertook,
as detailed in the Notice of Motion, and in particular what steps
should be taken to fully explore the most resilient and
cost effective manner of replacing
selected elements of the services they provided, be
noted;
 
(2)      
That authority be delegated to the Head of
Housing, Revenues and Customer Services to prepare a detailed
proposal describing how this could be achieved and at what cost, as
part of the forthcoming budget setting process;

 
(3)      
That enquiries be made with the five other
Warwickshire authorities to establish their approach to addressing
the service gaps created by the demise of WRCC;

 
(4)      
That the important role that Warm Hubs played
within local communities be recognised and the need to sustain them
in the interim, a budget of £25,000 be established from the
Business Rates Equalisation Reserve, which warm hubs could apply to
for funding to maintain and enhance their provision;
and

 
(5)      
That consultation be carried out with the
proposer and seconder of the Notice of Motion, alongside any
appropriate partners.
 
Note: This item is not subject to call-in as it is a
recommendation to Council
 
Councillor Cowcher returned to the meeting at this
juncture.

purpose:
Stratford-on-Avon District
Council funded component (£1.1m).
content:
Stratford-on-Avon District
Council funded component (£1.1m).

To implement robust parameters
when using the Stratford District Council funding for Warm Homes
Local Grant whilst retaining the ability to vary the DESNZ cost
caps when needed. We will vary the cost cap parameters from the
guidelines set by the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero
for Warm Homes Local Grant, for properties treated using Council
funds. This will enable the Council to upgrade properties which
would not be treatable under DESNZ guidelines. However, to avoid
disincentivising the DESNZ funded activity we will implement
stricter criteria under which these variations of the cost cap are
acceptable.
 

The Warm Homes Local Grant
(WHLG) is a Department of Energy Security and Net Zero (DESNZ)
funded programme which runs from April 2025 for at least three
years.
 
The Council has supplemented
the three-year £700,000 allocation from DESNZ by awarding
additional funding of £1,100,000 to the WHLG programme, to be
spent over the three years 2025/6 – 2027/8. Utilising Council
discretion to modify the cost cap parameters for this portion of
the funding enables the scheme to benefit residents whose
properties would be untreatable (or treatable to a lesser extent)
under DESNZ guidelines.
 
The DESNZ guidelines state
that:
Warm
Homes: Local Grant will have twin cost caps – one for energy
performance upgrades and one for low carbon heating.
 

 
Combining the two £15,000
caps into one single cost cap of £30,000 – which can be
spent on either energy performance upgrades and/or low carbon
heating continues to be the most effective way of delivering
measures for these homes, however, in practice, due to the
increased flexibility in the SDC funding it has been found to
create a significant inequality between the two funding streams and
creates a risk of over incentivising the Stratford DC funding (as a
result of its additional beneficial impact on the extent to which
the applicant can benefit) and disincentivising residents from
applying for the DESNZ allocation, with the risk of not spending
this and therefore returning it to DESNZ.
 
To mitigate the significant
risk of not meeting our MNZH/DESNZ contractual spending
requirements, we will introduce an enhanced set of criteria for
accessing the Stratford DC funded element of the grant.
 
The following conditions will
apply when administering the Stratford DC funding:
 
All applications will be
subject to the same rules as the MNZH/DESNZ funding stream
(£15,000 energy performance cost cap and £15,000 clean
heat cost cap) unless they meet one of the following
criteria:
 
1)  
There are no major works/significant measures (see
table below) recommended by the retrofit assessment that fit within
either of the DESNZ cost caps. (For example, that the only
recommended measure is an Air Source Heat Pump or External Wall
Insulation and not Solar PV and this exceeds a DESNZ cost
cap)
2)  
The property is a Park Home, on a residential site
and where it is impossible to install EWI/IWI and other ancillary
measures (see definition below) within the DESNZ cost
caps.
3)  
The property is a listed building or falls within a
conservation area – in this instance access to extra funding
will only be used to meet the needs of the planning consent and not
to gain extra measures.
4)  
The property has no existing central heating or
storage heating; the applicant qualifies for WHLG and therefore
there is a significant need for a full heating system
installation.
5)  
The installation is replacing a highly polluting
and/or high costly oil fired (or LPG) heating system with a clean
energy solution (ASHP or ESH), and no alternative mains gas supply
exists in the community or the
participant does not have sufficient income to fund a connection to
the existing gas supply. NOTE: WHLG scheme guidance does not
require an assessment of savings, only income – we are
proposing to adopt an identical approach to unsure that scheme
guidance does not become overly complicated.
 




Works Designation Table – Warm Homes Local
Grant




Major works/significant measures


Minor/ancillary measures




Solar PV


Loft insulation




External/Internal Wall
Insulation (EWI/IWI)


Heating controls




Air Source Heat Pump


Hot water cylinder
thermostat




High Heat Retention Storage
heaters


Digital/smart controls (Only in
conjunction with ASHP)




Park home insulation


Draft proofing (can only be
installed with Loft insulation)




 


Ventilation




 


Loft boarding and fire system
installation (Only in conjunction with Solar PV
installation)




 


Low energy lighting




 


Cavity wall
insulation




 
Given the experience of the
team in delivering the scheme in a large rural district we would
also seek to enable delegated authority to be provided to the
HoS and Housing and Communities Manager
to authorise awards where justifiable in any other circumstances
deemed exceptional – Wholly at the discretion of Stratford
DC. Communities and Social Inclusion Manager and Housing
Sustainability Project Officer decision with sign-off through
Housing and Communities Manager and review through Head of
Service.
topline: The Stratford-on-Avon District Council has decided to implement robust parameters for using council funding for the Warm Homes Local Grant, while retaining the ability to vary cost caps for properties treated using council funds.

purpose:

deed of variation.
content:
To grant the underlease and
deed of variation.
 

To approve the grant of an
underlease of the south parcel of Studley Leisure Centre (Pool
Road) to Sports and Leisure Management Limited (operating as
Everyone Active) in order to reflect the already established
operational arrangements, and to approve the associated deed of
variation to the existing lease of the north parcel to ensure the
two arrangements are aligned, including the linked termination
provisions.
 

The decision is made to
formally regularise a longstanding operational arrangement that has
been in place since the award of the leisure operating contract in
July 2021.
 
The leisure operating contract,
approved by Cabinet in November 2019, clearly envisaged that Sports
and Leisure Management Limited would occupy and operate facilities
across both the north and south parcels of Studley Leisure Centre.
While a lease was completed for the north parcel, the underlease of
the south parcel was not executed at that time due to an
administrative oversight.
 
Sports and Leisure Management
Limited has nevertheless occupied and operated both the swimming
pool (north parcel) and sports hall (south parcel) continuously in
accordance with the contract. The proposed underlease and deed of
variation therefore do not introduce a new arrangement but instead
formalise the position that was intended by the parties and has
existed in practice since 2021.
 
The documentation has been
prepared in line with the agreed lease template appended to the
leisure operating contract, with terms aligned to ensure
consistency between the north and south parcels, including mutual
termination provisions.
 
Regularising the position
ensures legal clarity, reflects the contractual intent, and
supports the continued effective operation of the leisure
centre.
 

1.  
Do nothing – Not
recommended, as this would leave an inconsistency between the legal
documentation and the operational reality, creating potential legal
and governance risks.
2.  
Seek separate specific authority outside existing
arrangements – Considered
unnecessary given that the proposed documentation merely formalises
the position envisaged and approved as part of the leisure
operating contract.
3.  
Approve the underlease and deed of variation
(preferred option) – Ensures legal
alignment with the intended and established contractual and
operational position, providing clarity and certainty for all
parties.
topline: The Deputy Chief Executive has decided to grant an underlease and deed of variation for the south parcel of Studley Leisure Centre to Sports and Leisure Management Limited.

content:
That the District Council award through grant
funding £20,000 to the Parenting Project for continuation of
their work in Upper Lighthorne to support Lighthorne Heath Primary
School and residents.

Lighthorne Heath Primary School previously
approached Stratford-on-Avon District Council because of an
increase in children attending the school due to the expansion of
housing in the local area. A number of these children were from
households with additional needs/ challenges that required support
which the school was finding challenging to meet. Often these were
families housed through the Council’s housing allocations
process. From this an action was added to the Growing Opportunities

decision_maker: Head of Environmental and Operational Services
content:
To procure and award contract
to SFG20.
 


In order
to satisfy statutory compliance requirements, assets
within SDC’s estate require inspection and survey on a set
frequency (commonly known as Pre-Planned Maintenance, or
PPM).  However, the assets that require
this are not all captured, and those that have limited data
recorded.  This means that the
scheduling of these inspections and surveys is sporadic at best,
and realistically not covering all assets that are required under
statutory compliance.  This puts SDC at
risk of legislative breaches that could result in financial and
reputational damage should an incident occur.

There is therefore the need to identify
all assets within the estate that we have direct responsibility for
e.g. excluding leased properties.  There
is also a requirement to record the associated data, such as
manufacturer, make, model, capacity, rating, condition
etc.

Once asset data is obtained, it can then
be reviewed and the type of PPM, and frequency,
determined.  Once a schedule has been
created, it can be issued to market for competitive pricing with
the intention of appointing a single provider.  This provider can then start to carry out the
PPM’s and associated service reports / recommendations and
SDC can then procure necessary repairs / maintenance /
replacement.

SFG20 will survey our properties (excluding open air
car parks and Windsor Street car park) to identify all assets and
collate associated data.  They will
apply a ‘tag’ to each asset comprising a QR code, so
when this is scanned, it brings up all
of the associated data for the asset.

SFG20 will also determine what PPM’s are needed, the associated specification
and time required to complete.  It will
also produce a schedule based upon the type of asset and required
PPM, including the frequency.  Such
frequencies can be as short as monthly, so the schedule would be
too complicated for SDC to produce themselves, especially as the
number of assets could be over a thousand.

The PPM specifications, frequencies and associated
time required will form the basis of the procurement and allow
bidders to price with accuracy, realism and certainty, whilst also
allowing SDC to evaluate with consistency and
confidence.  This will ensure that the
‘correct’ bidder will be appointed and VFM evaluated
and achieved.

The data will be hosted on SFG20 cloud-based
software, however, an API will be
written to allow two-way transfer of data with our recently
procured Computer Aided Facilities Management software,
Jellyhaus. 
SFG20 is a secondary system to Jellyhaus and is not intended for use as the
primary mechanism for SDC to manage its assets.

Of note is that as the schedules that specify the
PPM’s is part of the fee proposal, it can be decided which
PPM’s are carried out by in-house
staff, and they will have an industry standard specification to
follow to ensure compliance.  This will
lead to cost savings as the quantity of PPM’s in the procurement via the market can be
reduced.

The procurement of this product and service is the
key enabler to delivering SDC’s asset management strategy and
ensure legal compliance at all times
going forward.

Although there are several companies in existence
that offer similar products, none offer the depth and detail that
SFG20 does.  For example, Smartlog provides a portal to store assets and
associated data, including PPM frequency, however, it does not
produce PPM schedules with associated time requirements, nor do
they survey and tag assets to identify them and capture relevant
data and condition. In fact, Smartlog
is described as “… a
user-friendly online health & safety compliance management
system that allows for the monitoring and auditing of all of your
health & safety policies and
procedures.”

Asset management is only a small part of their
software and does not match SFG20 in their product
offer.

 
 

1.  
Award to SFG20.
2.  
Aborting the project.
topline: The Head of Environmental and Operational Services has decided to procure and award a contract to SFG20 for asset inspection and survey to ensure statutory compliance and prevent financial and reputational damage.

decision_maker: Head of Environmental and Operational Services
content:
To procure and award contract
to Higham Roofing and Construction.


 

The intention was for Solar PV to be installed to the roof at the
Leisure Centre in Summer 2026.  However,
following a raft of surveys it was noted that the felt flat roof
had blistered.  There was also evidence
of localised internal water penetration.

 

Blistering flat roofs are quite often a result of moisture being
trapped within the build-up and turning to vapour in warm and hot
conditions.  Thus, a moisture map survey
was procured that has showed numerous areas of roof build-up being
saturated.  This therefore explained why
the roof had blistered and why water staining was evident
internally.

 

The roof has failed and is beyond repair meaning that the Solar PV
installation cannot proceed.  It would
be folly to install such a system on a failed roof, as the cost of
removing and reinstalling the PV in several years would be
wasteful.

 

The preference would be to execute these roofing works as soon as
possible, however, the small parking area at the Centre (relative
to numbers of users and staff) means that taking spaces out of use
for contractor compound is not possible.  Several options to avoid this have been explored,
such as a ‘remote’ compound; leisure centre staff
parking on the roads; staff parking at The Grange Hall, however,
all have been discounted as being either unsafe or anti-social.

 

Of particular note is that there is an agreement in place with the
adjoining school whereby their car park can be used by the Centre
when they are not in session.  Thus, the
six week school shutdown is the ideal time to carry out this work
(the Solar PV installation is now scheduled for Summer 2027 for the
same reasons).

 

The preferred supplier for the roofing work has stated that they
can deliver the works in this 6 week period provided they get an
order by 19th June 2026. 
This then allows mobilisation time for materials delivery and
satisfaction of health and safety (CDM) requirements.

 

In order to try and understand the limitations of the contractor
base / market dialogue was started with Higham Roofing and
Construction several weeks ago.  It has
allowed us to ascertain without doubt that it is impossible to
produce an ITT and tender to the market between now and June (when
any contractor would need an order to allow for mobilisation and
CDM requirements etc.).

 

If the window of Summer 2026 is missed for this work, then it
can’t happen until Summer 2027, and the Solar PV will have to
be further delayed to 2028.  This is
very negative for SDC’s reputation and delays the carbon
reduction benefits that the scheme will bring.  It also increases price risk given current and
predicted inflation rates.

 

Surveys were commissioned at pace once the blistering roof had been
identified in March 2026, with the moisture map and specification
being received late the week of 4th May 2026.


Award to Higham
Roofing and Construction; or
Aborting the
project.
topline: The Head of Environmental and Operational Services has decided to award the contract to Higham Roofing and Construction for roofing works at a Leisure Centre, including the installation of Solar PV.

Economic Development Portfolio
 
Consideration was given to an
assessment of the Core Strategy policies against the provisions of
the current National Planning Policy Framework (NPPF) in order to ascertain their current level of
conformity with national policy. Local Planning Authorities were
required to carry out a review of their local plan policies at
least once every five years in order to
determine whether or not they required
updating.
 
In receiving the report, it was
noted that whilst the assessment had concluded that most of the
policies within the Core Strategy remained relevant and could be
afforded weight by the Council in reaching planning decisions, in
some key respects, notably in relation to housing land supply, some
policies would need to be considered out of date.
 
The options available to The
Cabinet were:
 

1.  
To recommend that the assessment on the continued
conformity of Core Strategy policies against the provisions of the
NPPF, as set out in Appendix 1 of the agenda report, be formally
endorsed, and that the Core Strategy remained partially up to date
and continued in part to provide an appropriate basis on which to
plan for Stratford-on-Avon District to 2031;
 

2.  
To amend the assessment on the continued general
conformity of Core Strategy policies against the provisions of the
NPPF and recommend Council endorsed an amended version;
or
 

3.  
Not to recommend that the assessment be formally
endorsed and conclude that the Core Strategy was no longer up to
date.
 
Councillor Crump, Chair of the
Overview and Scrutiny Committee (OSC), provided feedback from the
meeting held on 8 April 2026. He noted that although some Council
policies were considered up to date, they could still be challenged
and potentially deemed out of date at appeal. While this assessment
would have been required in any event, it was closely linked to the
District’s lack of a five-year
housing land supply and the emerging South Warwickshire Local Plan
(SWLP). In relation to policies identified as out of date, it was
noted that the Council was focusing on restoring the five-year
housing land supply and progressing the SWLP in line with agreed
timescales, in order to strengthen its
policy position going forward.
 
Accordingly, it was
 
RECOMMENDED
to Council:
 
That the
findings of the review assessment, as detailed in Appendix 1 of the
agenda report, outlining which Core Strategy policies were

content:
Councillor Coles - Housing and Customer Services
Portfolio
 
Consideration was given to the
final Housing Allocations Scheme for approval
following completion of public and stakeholder
consultation.
 
In receiving the report, it was
noted that the Housing Allocations Scheme had been developed to
support the Council’s ambitions set out in its Housing
Strategy, including the prevention and reduction of homelessness
and the effective use of housing stock through collaborative
working with Registered Providers. It was further noted that a
clear Allocations Scheme provided clarity for applicants and
supported the Council in meeting housing needs by prioritising
access to social housing for those in greatest need.
 
The options available to The
Cabinet were to endorse the Housing Allocations Scheme, to amend
the Housing Allocations Scheme and then endorse, or not endorse the
Housing Allocations Scheme.
 
Councillor Crump, Chair of the
Overview and Scrutiny Committee (OSC), provided feedback from the
meeting held on 8 April 2026, and confirmed that the OSC would
conduct a review of the new IT system, which was being implemented
alongside the Scheme after twelve months.
 
Following which, it
was
 
RECOMMENDED
to Council:
 
(1) 
That the Housing Allocations Scheme, as detailed
in Appendix 1 to the agenda report, be endorsed;

 
(2) 
That authority be delegated to the Head of
Housing, Revenues and Customer Services to take the necessary steps
to implement the decision; and

 
(3) 
That authority be delegated to the Head of
Housing, Revenues and Customer Services, in consultation with the
Portfolio Holder, to make minor amendments to the Housing
Allocations Scheme.
 
Note: This item is not subject to call-in to the OSC as the item
is subject to a recommendation to Council.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to endorse the final Housing Allocations Scheme to support the Council's housing strategy and prioritize access to social housing for those in greatest need.

content:
Councillor Juned – Leader
of the Council
 
Consideration was given to the
allocation of funds from the Climate Change Reserve to the
Community Climate Change and Nature Recovery Fund and the Wilder
Communities Project.
 
In receiving the report, it was
noted that funds for Round Four were being requested due to the
recent successes of the first three rounds of the Community Climate
Change and Nature Recovery Fund.
 
It was further noted that
applications relating to the agreed sites and eligible for the
Wilder Communities Project 2026/27 would be subject to consultation
with the relevant organisations prior to approval by the Appraisal
Group.
 
The options available to The
Cabinet were:
 

1.  
To approve the recommendations, as set out in the
agenda report, with £200,000 allocated from the Climate
Change Reserve to the Community Climate Change and Nature Recovery
Fund;

2.  
To recommend that the mechanisms for delivery be
amended prior to £200,000 allocated from the Climate Change
Reserve to the Community Climate Change and Nature Recovery
Fund;

3.  
To approve the allocation of £200,000 from the
Climate Change Reserve to the budget for Round Four of the
Community Climate Change and Nature Recovery Fund, but not approve
the allocation of £22,500 to the Wilder Communities
Project;

4.  
To approve the allocation of £22,500 from the
Climate Change Reserve to the budget for the Wilder Communities
Project, but not approve the allocation of £200,000 to Round
Four of the Community Climate Change and Nature Recovery Fund;
or

5.  
Not to approve the allocation of £200,000 from
the Climate Change Reserve to the Community Climate Change and
Nature Recovery Fund or £22,500 to the Wilder Communities
Project.
 
Accordingly, it was
 
RESOLVED:
 
(1)  That the
Community Climate Change and Nature Recovery Fund be re-established
for a Fourth Round;

 
(2)  That a total
budget of £200,000 be allocated from the Climate Change
Reserve to the Community Climate Change and Nature Recovery
Fund;
 
(3)  That
applications be appraised and approved using the process set out in
the agenda report and that the application window be open for a
period of twelve months, with funds distributed on a quarterly
basis;

 
(4)  That the Wilder
Communities Project be re-established for the 2026/27 financial
year, and that £22,500 be allocated to the Project from the
Climate Change Reserve; and
 
(5)  That the Deputy
Chief Executive, in consultation with the Leader of the Council,
continue to have delegated authority to approve projects funded by
both programmes.
 
Note: This item is not subject to call-in to the OSC as it is
not a key decision.
topline: The Council has decided to allocate funds from the Climate Change Reserve to the Community Climate Change and Nature Recovery Fund and the Wilder Communities Project.

content:

responses to in relation to proposals for local government
reorganisation in Warwickshire are agreed, as follows:

Stratford on Avon District Council formal response in relation to

Council for one unitary council; and

Stratford-on-Avon District Council and Warwick District

To amend the proposed consultation responses

To reject the proposed consultation responses
attached at Appendix 1 and Appendix 2.

To not respond to the consultation.

decision_maker: Head of Housing, Revenues and Customer Services
content:
That the District Council award
through grant funding £36,666 to Citizens Advice South
Warwickshire for a contribution towards their core
services.
 

Stratford-on-Avon District
Council has a long-standing commitment to fund Citizens Advice
South Warwickshire.
 
Citizens Advice South
Warwickshire is a charity operating within the district and
delivering free confidential and impartial advice on a range of
subjects including housing, benefits, debt, fuel poverty,
education, law & rights and health. Their help is available to
everyone in the community.
 
CASW is a key partner, and
their activities are aligned to the Growing Opportunities Plan
2026-29. The Council has historically supported CASW by
contributing towards its core costs.
 
From CASW’s Q3 report for
25-26 they have supported residents to manage £1,039,807 of
debt, gain £1,177,947 and write off £226,094 of
debt.
 

Several factors have been taken
into account and the following has been
considered in reaching this decision:
 

Whether the budget
allows for these grant awards.
Whether the
organisation is appropriately qualified to undertake this
work.
Whether these
organisations delivered this work within the district and
effectively with the 2025/26 award.
Whether this work is
aligned with the Growing Opportunities and Council
Plans.
Whether a need exists
for this activity and spending.

 
The answer to all of these questions is
‘yes’.
topline: The Head of Housing, Revenues and Customer Services has decided to award £36,666 in grant funding to Citizens Advice South Warwickshire for their core services.

decision_maker: Head of Housing, Revenues and Customer Services
content:
That the District Council award
through grant funding £108,593 to Citizens Advice South
Warwickshire for the enhanced Court Desk Worker service for
26-27.
 

Stratford-on-Avon District
Council has previously commissioned Citizens Advice South
Warwickshire (CASW) to deliver the Court Desk Worker service to
assist residents in the district when faced with possession orders
from landlords which could lead to homelessness without appropriate
support and representation.
 
The Court Desk Worker service
represents clients in court during possession hearings, runs
pre-court surgeries for tenants, supports access to other
specialist services to tackle other issues clients face, supports
clients to negotiate sustainable mortgage or rent payment plans
with landlords and lenders. This service is provided to residents
free of charge.
 
Last year Orbit gave notice on
the Tenancy Intervention Officer contract which was a key role in
working alongside the Court Desk Worker. This meant the pre-work,
previously carried out by the Tenancy Intervention Officer before
referring to the Court Desk Worker, was no longer being done.
Additional resource was directed to the Court Desk Worker service
to meet this gap which has proved beneficial.
 
With the additional capacity
the outputs were increased whilst also acknowledging the increased
demand from more residents facing eviction. From the Quarter 3
25/26 report, the Court Desk Worker service has supported 279
clients against a target for the year of 330 (85%), prevented 201
cases of residents threatened with homelessness against a target of
260 (77%) and supported clients with a £730,800 income gain
(arrears addressed, debt managed/ written off/ benefit application,
etc) against a target of £600k (122%). This has meant 201
residents/ families have been able to remain in their homes which
prevents a lot of work/ support by SDC colleagues if they must be
managed as homeless. Also, importantly it prevents significant
negative impact on the household which can mean long term
challenges from being displaced.
 
CASW is a charity operating
within the district delivering free confidential and impartial
advice on a range of subjects including housing, benefits, debt,
fuel poverty, education, law & rights and health. Their help is
available to everyone in the community.
 
CASW is a key partner, and
their activities are aligned to the Growing Opportunities Plan
2026-29.
 
The required amount of
£108,593 pa will be funded in the following way:
 
£38,000 is assigned to
CASW court desk work from the core budget.
 
£70,593 will be allocated
from the Homeless Prevention Grant.
 

Several factors have been taken
into account and the following has been
considered in reaching this decision:
 

Whether the budget
allows for these grant awards.
Whether the
organisation is appropriately qualified to undertake this
work.
Whether these
organisations delivered this work within the district and
effectively with the 2025/26 award.
Whether this work is
aligned with the Growing Opportunities and Council
Plans.
Whether a need exists
for this activity and spending.

 
The answer to all these
questions is ‘yes’.
topline: The Head of Housing, Revenues and Customer Services has decided to award grant funding to Citizens Advice South Warwickshire for an enhanced Court Desk Worker service to assist residents facing eviction and homelessness.

content:
Councillor Cowcher – Deputy Leader – Planning and
Economic Development Portfolio
 
Consideration was given to the
latest timescale for the preparation of the Council’s Local
Plan documents, as set out in the revised Local Development Scheme
(LDS).
 
Stratford-on-Avon District
Councils LDS was published in March 2025 and was required to be
reviewed regularly to ensure it was kept up-to-date and reflected
the current and anticipated work programme. It was noted that Local
Plan must be prepared in accordance with the published LDS and were
also required to be formally adopted by the Council in accordance
with Section 15(7) of the Planning and Compulsory Purchase Act 2004
(as amended).
 
The options available to The
Cabinet were to agree the updated timetable and adopt the updated
LDS, to amend the LDS and then adopt it, or not to adopt the
updated LDS and to retain the existing LDS.
 
It was noted that officers had
considered the position of the Site Allocations Plan (SAP) in
relation to the LDS update, and had concluded that it was the
appropriate time to cease any further work on the SAP and formally
withdraw it once the public consultation on the South Warwickshire
Local Plan Publication (Regulation 19) document commenced, on the
basis that the Regulation 19 version of the South Warwickshire
Local Plan would sufficiently cover the relevant content of the
latest Preferred Options version of the SAP.
 
Following which, it
was
 
RECOMMENDED
to Council:
 
(1) 
That the timetable for the preparation of Local
Plan documents, as outlined in the agenda report, be approved and
that the Stratford-on-Avon District Local Development Scheme be
revised accordingly;
 
(2) 
That the Site Allocations Plan be withdrawn from
the Local Development Scheme on the date that the South
Warwickshire Local Plan Publication (Regulation 19) document
commences public consultation and no longer be progressed as a
Development Plan Document by the Council; and
 
(3) 
That the revised Local Development Scheme be
brought into effect in accordance with Section 15(7) of the
Planning and Compulsory Purchase Act 2004 (as
amended).
 
Note: This item is not subject to call-in to the OSC as the item
is subject to a recommendation to Council.
topline: The Council has decided to approve the updated timetable for Local Plan documents and withdraw the Site Allocations Plan.

content:
Councillor Grocott - Environmental and Neighbourhood Services
Portfolio
 
Consideration was given to the
adoption of the Stratford-on-Avon Air Quality Strategy.
 
In receiving the report, it was
noted that Stratford?on?Avon District
Council had declared two Air Quality Management Areas (AQMAs) in
Stratford?upon?Avon and
Studley for exceedances of the Nitrogen Dioxide air quality
objective. Improvements in air quality in both areas had led to the
revocation of the AQMAs in October 2025. It was further noted that
the improvement in air quality had primarily resulted from reduced
nitrogen oxide emissions due to cleaner vehicle technology,
alongside the impact of initiatives relating to active transport,
traffic management, road infrastructure, and planning
policy.
 
The options available to The
Cabinet were to adopt or not to adopt the Stratford-on-Avon Air
Quality Strategy.
 
A question was raised regarding
the costs and implications of the Strategy. The Head of

content:
The Leader’s Decision
Report (26 February 2026) recommends approval of the procurement of
a provider and the grant of a lease to enable the scheme to operate
in line with the business case and support the Council’s
prevention first approach to homelessness. Authority is delegated
to the Head of Housing, Revenues & Customer Services, in
consultation with Head of Law and Governance, to finalise and
complete the contractual documents and lease
arrangements.

To approve the procurement of a
provider to operate 1 Evesham Place as supported accommodation,
including:
 

procurement of
housing management and support services, and
the grant of a 5?year
lease to the successful provider to enable the delivery of those
services.

 
This decision is taken under
delegated authority to finalise and enter
into the required contractual and lease
arrangements.

1
Evesham Place has been acquired, reconfigured and refurbished to
create a six?unit
supported accommodation scheme for single people who are homeless
or at risk of homelessness and who require low to medium levels of
accommodation?based
support.
The
refurbishment has transformed the former nine?bedroom HMO into self?contained units with communal and support
spaces, meeting HMO and fire safety standards.
To
realise the strategic and financial benefits of the approved
business case and reduce reliance on hotel and guest house
accommodation. The Council must now put in place suitable
operational arrangements. Procurement of a specialist provider,
operating under a concession?style model, enables:

·        
delivery of housing management, repairs, maintenance
and support services.

·        
operation via exempt accommodation rental and
service charge income.

·        
transfer of day to day
operational risk to the provider while the Council retains asset
ownership.

·        
compliance with the Supported Housing (Regulatory
Oversight) Act 2023 and National Supported Housing
Standards.
The Leaders Decision (26
February 2026) approves the procurement approach and the grant of a
lease, with authority delegated to the Head of Housing, Revenues
& Customer Services to complete all necessary
arrangements.

Option 1 – Approve the procurement and lease
(chosen)
This option enables 1 Evesham Place to open as supported
accommodation, delivering improved outcomes for vulnerable single
people and reducing the Council’s dependence on costly
B&B accommodation.
 
Option 2 – Do not proceed
This would leave a fully refurbished but empty building, result in
ongoing running costs without benefit and fail to reduce B&B
use or support homelessness prevention.
topline: The Leader has decided to approve the procurement of a provider and the grant of a lease to operate a supported accommodation scheme for homeless individuals.

content:
Councillor Gist – Law and Governance Portfolio (presented
by Councillor Juned – Leader of the Council in the absence of
Councillor Gist)
 
Consideration was given to the
future use of The Grange Hall, Southam.
 
In receiving the report, it was
noted that the land was jointly owned by Stratford-on-Avon District
Council (SDC) and Southam Town Council (STC). Grange Hall had been
operated by STC as a community facility for the benefit of the
residents of Southam until Autumn 2024, when it was closed to
undergo refurbishments and was currently mothballed. STC had
confirmed that it did not intend to return to use it as an
operational asset.
 
In addition, as part of the
agreed management arrangements for Grange Hall, a Stewards Panel
was in existence, comprising of representatives from SDC and STC,
to oversee day-to-day operation. Under the Constitution of Grange
Hall, decisions regarding its future were reserved to SDC and STC,
and not the Stewards, therefore as Grange Hall was no longer an
operating asset, it was proposed that the Stewards Panel be
disbanded, on the agreement of both SDC and STC.
 
The options available to The
Cabinet were to
 

1)  
Support Option 1, as set out in the agenda report,
to sell the Grange Hall;

2)  
Support Option 2, as set out in the agenda report,
to advertise the Grange Hall for lease by commercial organisations;
or

3)  
Support Option 3, as set out in the agenda report,
to advertise the Grange Hall for use as a Community
Asset.
 
During the discussion,
Councillor Adam noted the keenness of residents and STC to use
Grange Hall as a community asset. Councillor Coles added that
should this option prove to be unsuccessful, then Option 1 to
become the fallback position.
 
Councillor Crump, Chair of
Overview and Scrutiny Committee (OSC) provided feedback from the
meeting of the OSC held on 4 February 2026 and noted that STC had
requested timescales for Option 3, which was noted.
 
Following which, it
was
 
RESOLVED:
 
(1)That Option 3, to
advertise the Grange Hall for use as a community asset, be
agreed;
 
(2)  That, in
conjunction with the agreement of Southam Town Council, the Grange
Hall Stewards be disbanded; and
 
(3)  That the Deputy
Chief Executive, in consultation with the Portfolio Holder for Law
and Governance and the Monitoring Officer, be authorised to
complete the due diligence, legal agreements and documentation
required to implement these decisions.
 
Note: In accordance with the Council’s Constitution, this
item is not subject to call-in to the OSC.
topline: The Council has decided to advertise The Grange Hall for use as a community asset.

content:
Councillor Curtis – Resources
Portfolio
 
Consideration was given to a
report detailing the expected activities of the Council’s
Treasury function in the financial year 2026/27, including the
Prudential Indicators, in relation to Treasury Management for
2026/27 and beyond. In addition, the Annual Investment Strategy
detailed the investment instruments available to the Council and
proposed which of these instruments the Council
utilised.
 
The Council had an obligation
when considering the Budget to take into account the Prudential
Code and set the Prudential Indicators, whether or not it decided
to borrow. The Code did not include any suggested limits or ratios,
as this would be for the Council to set, subject to any controls
under Section 4 of the Local Government Act 2003.
 
The Prudential Code laid down
clear governance procedures for setting and revising Prudential
Indicators, with the S151 Officer bearing the responsibility
for:
 

·      
Ensuring that the Council had taken into account all
matters specified by the Code; and

·      
Monitoring compliance with established limits
approved by full Council before the beginning of each financial
year.
 
In setting or revising the
Indicators, the Council was required to have regard to the
following matters:
 

·      
Affordability, e.g. implications for Council
Tax;

·      
Prudence and sustainability, e.g. implications for
external borrowing;

·      
Value for money, e.g. options appraisals;

·      
Stewardship of assets, e.g. asset management
planning;

·      
Service objectives, e.g. strategic planning for the
Council; and

·      
Practicality, e.g. achievability of the Forward
Plan.
 
The options available to The
Cabinet were to:
 

1.  
Accept the 2026/27 Treasury Strategy Statement as
recommended, or amend the Strategy or its limits as appropriate;
and
 

2.  
Approve the Annual Investment Strategy for 2026/27
as recommended, or amend as appropriate.
 
Accordingly, it was
 
RECOMMENDED
to Council:
 
(1)      
That the 2026/27 Treasury Management Strategy
Statement, attached as Appendix 1 to the agenda report, be endorsed
and the following limits be set for:
 
a) 
The overall borrowing limit, £25m;
and
b) 
The short-term borrowing limit
£16m.
 
(2)      
That the proposed Prudential Indicators for
2026/27, contained within Appendix 1, be approved;
 
(3)      
That the Minimum Revenue Provision (MRP) policy
statement, as set out in Section 2 of Appendix 1 to the agenda
report, be approved;
 
(4)      
That the Annual Investment Strategy for 2026/27,
as set out in Section 4 of Appendix 1 to the agenda report, be
approved; and
 
(5)      
That the Capital Strategy 2026/27 –
2030/31, as set out in Appendix 2 to the agenda report, be
approved.
 
Note:
This item is not subject to call-in to the OSC as the item is
subject to a recommendation to Council.
topline: The Council has decided to approve the Treasury Management Strategy Statement, Prudential Indicators, Minimum Revenue Provision policy statement, Annual Investment Strategy, and Capital Strategy for the financial year 2026/27.

report.
 
In considering the report, The
Cabinet was required to address corporate governance issues as
required under the provisions of the Local Government Act 2003.
These were summarised as follows:
 
Adequacy of Reserves
 
The Chief Financial Officer had
a duty to report on the adequacy of the proposed financial reserves
when the budget was being considered. The desired level of revenue
balances, as determined by the Chief Financial Officer was
£3.0 million for 2026/27, and as agreed in the Reserves
Strategy approved by The Cabinet in January 2026 (Minute 463
refers), the position in relation to the Council’s General
Fund Reserve figure would be reviewed annually. The actual level of
reserves as at 31 March 2026 was still
to be determined, however, it was estimated to be around
£17.3 million. The estimated position of the General Fund
Reserves over the next five years was summarised in the
MTFS.
 
Robustness of
Estimates
 
The Chief Financial Officer had
a specific duty to report on the robustness of estimates in the
budget proposals when the budget was being considered. The Cabinet
acknowledged that a rigorous process and timetable had been
followed throughout the Budget setting process this year and all
key assumptions used had been reviewed and scrutinised as part of
this process.
 
The options available to The
Cabinet were to approve or amend any of the proposals.
 
In considering the report, The
Cabinet acknowledged that the Council had undertaken a
comprehensive review of the Medium-Term Financial Strategy to
arrive at a five-year budget plan that met the corporate priorities
of the Council.
 
Councillor Crump, Chair of the
Overview and Scrutiny Committee (OSC) provided feedback from the
meeting of the OSC held on 4 February 2026 and noted the increased
charges of fly-tipped waste collection and the decrease in
overnight car parking charges at Council run carparks. OSC members
requested that with future budgets, any significant increases or
decreases in spending or charging be accompanied with a brief
narrative to explain the change.
 
In response to a query
regarding whether the monies used for the Stratford-upon-Avon
Leisure Centre Solar Panels scheme should have formed part of the
budget consultations, it was confirmed that the money used for the
solar panel installations had been from the Climate Change budget
from the previous year.
 
Accordingly, it was
 
RECOMMENDED
to Council:
 
(1)  
That the proposed Medium Term Capital Programme,
detailed at Appendix 4 to the agenda report, be agreed;
 
(2)  
That the proposed Medium Term Revenue Budget,
detailed at Appendix 6 to the agenda report be approved;
and
 
(3)  
That the level of Council Tax be set at
£174.18 for a Band D property for 2026/27.

 

RESOLVED:

 
(1)       
That the proposals for fees and charges, detailed at
Appendix 5 to the agenda report, be approved; and
 
(2)       
That the Non-Domestic Rates provisional
contributions for 2026/27, as detailed in the NNDR1 form at
Appendix 7 to the agenda report, be approved.
 
Note: Recommendations 1 to 3 are not subject to call-in as the
matter is subject to recommendation to Council.  In accordance with the Council’s
Constitution, Resolutions 1 and 2 are not subject to call-in to the
OSC.
topline: The Council has decided to approve the Medium Term Capital Programme, Revenue Budget, Council Tax level, fees and charges, and Non-Domestic Rates contributions for 2026/27.

content:
To consider Public space
CCTV

That a public consultation will take place to consider the
installation of public space CCTV in Summerton Way,
Stratford-upon-Avon.

Stratford-on-Avon District
Council has been aware of concerns from residents about anti-social
behaviour taking place around the alleyways near the scout hut and
the top end of Summerton Way. As a result the council have worked closely with
Warwickshire Police to address these concerns. Funding obtained by
Warwickshire County Council through the Shared Prosperity Fund has
allowed for the opportunity for CCTV to be installed at this
location. As a part of this approach two new CCTV cameras are
proposed to be installed and monitored by the council’s CCTV
service. The purpose of these cameras would be to detect and
prevent crime and provide community reassurance.
 
In consideration of installing
CCTV the council wishes to consult with residents, nearby
businesses and community groups to obtain their views on the
proposal. Such consultation will also inform data privacy impact
assessments and ensure compliance with guidance from the
Information Commissioner and Surveillance Camera Commissioners
Office.
 
An online consultation will be
carried out for an 8-week period. Local resident’s businesses
and landowners near the proposed CCTV deployment will also be
written to seeking their views.

A number
of options were considered by the
Monitoring Officer, these included:
 

That the council
undertakes a public consultation on the proposal to install public
space CCTV in Summerton Way, Stratford-upon-Avon.

 

That the council does
not undertake a public consultation and withdraws its intention to
install CCTV at Summerton Way, Stratford-upon-Avon.
topline: The Head of Law and Governance and Monitoring Officer has decided to approve recommendations for a public consultation on installing public space CCTV in Summerton Way, Stratford-upon-Avon.

content:
To appoint a suitably qualified
Employer’s Agent who will also undertake the Contract
Administrator role for the Stratford Gateway demolition project,
with an estimated value of £10,000–£15,000, in
accordance with the Council’s Contract Procedure
Rules.

To progress the Stratford
Gateway demolition programme in a controlled and compliant way, the
Council requires the appointment of an Employer’s Agent who
will also act as the Contract Administrator.
 
This role is essential to
provide technical oversight across all pre?demolition and
demolition?related activities. It is also a legal requirement under
the JCT Minor Works contract form that a Contract Administrator is
formally appointed by the Client to administer the contract, issue
instructions, certify payments, and oversee compliance.
 
The Employer’s Agent
provides the specialist assurance needed to ensure that surveys,
statutory processes, technical designs, tender documentation,
contractor submissions and on?site activities are properly
validated and managed in accordance with legal, safety and
contractual requirements.
 
Without this appointment, the
Council would be unable to administer the demolition contract
lawfully or meet the technical and regulatory standards required to
deliver the programme.
 
The
Employer’s Agent will:

Oversee and validate
all pre?demolition surveys, including asbestos, ecology, utilities,
heritage, contaminated land, tree and arboriculture assessments
etc;
Provide technical
review and assurance of the demolition scope, methodology,
sequencing and the detailed demolition specification;
Support planning
processes, statutory notices and related regulatory requirements,
ensuring relevant permissions, conditions and dependencies are
addressed;
Coordinate and
technically oversee utilities disconnection activities, including
desktop searches, intrusive tracing and applications to utilities
providers;
Prepare, review and
finalise tender documentation, and lead the technical evaluation of
tender returns to ensure the Council receives a compliant and
value?for?money submission;
Provide assurance on
contractor submissions such as temporary works designs, method
statements, Construction Phase Plans, environmental plans, waste
and materials management strategies and traffic management
proposals;
Ensure all pre?start
compliance requirements are met ahead of site mobilisation,
including health and safety documentation, permits, licences and
regulatory checks;
Act as Contract
Administrator throughout mobilisation, demolition and completion,
administering the contract in accordance with JCT Minor Works
requirements and providing oversight of progress, quality,
compliance, risk and change control; and
Oversee delivery of
the interim post?demolition site condition, including the temporary
car park, fencing, security measures, land management and required
post?completion records.

 

·      
Proceed without an Employer’s
Agent:
Rejected. The Council does not have internal capacity or specialist
demolition technical expertise to undertake the required technical
checks, surveys management, specification drafting, tender
evaluation, and contract administration. The required JCT minor
works also requires a contract administrator as a Legal component.
Proceeding without an Employer’s Agent would significantly
increase risk and is not legally or operationally
viable.
 

Delay appointment
until Cabinet approval for demolition works:
Rejected. The pre?demolition programme (surveys, planning,
statutory notices, specification development and tendering)
requires immediate technical oversight. Delaying the appointment
would stall the programme and prevent the Council from reaching the
procurement and planning stages aligned with the
October–November 2026 demolition commencement
target.

 

Appoint
Employer’s Agent under delegated
authority:
Accepted. This is a low?value non?key decision and can be taken by
Officer Delegated Authority via this Notice of Officer Decision.
Appointment ensures compliance, maintains programme momentum, and
provides the technical assurance needed to advance the
project.  The outcome from this work
once authorised will inform the content of the Cabinet Report that
will follow in May or June next year in support of the Gateway
Demolition Programme.
topline: The Deputy Chief Executive has decided to appoint an Employer's Agent for the Stratford Gateway demolition project to ensure compliance and technical oversight.

content:
Note and endorse the
Warwickshire Community Safety Agreement for 2025-2029 

There is a duty under the Crime and Disorder
Act 1998 and its associated 2007 regulations for there to be a
countywide community safety strategy group. Within Warwickshire,
this group is called the Safer Warwickshire Partnership Board
(SWPB). Stratford-on-Avon District Council (SDC) is a member of the
SWPB alongside other district and borough councils in the County
and statutory agencies who are responsible for reducing crime and
anti-social behaviour. Within the Act is the requirement for the
countywide group to prepare a Community Safety Agreement (CSA). As
required by legislation, the CSA is based on the four comprehensive
Community Safety Partnership (CSP) strategic assessments undertaken
during 2024-25 and sets out how partner agencies in Warwickshire
will work together to implement shared community safety
priorities.
 
The CSA was presented to
the SWPB on 24 June 2025 and was approved subject to formal sign
off through partner agency governance processes.  
 
The Head of Law and Governance and Monitoring
Officer is delegated within the constitution to sign off such
agreements on behalf of Stratford District Council but brought the
agreement to the attention of the Senior Management Team on
23rd September 2025 before so approving.
 
Note- All Partner councils have recently
approved the agreement via their own governance and approval
processes as well.

A number of options were
considered by the Monitoring Officer
 
Option 1
- To note the Community Safety Agreement for
Warwickshire for 2025-2029 which the Monitoring Officer will sign
on SDC’s behalf as per delegations.
 
Option 2 – To suggest changes or further
information regarding the Community Safety Agreement before
signing. No changes were identified and therefore this option was
not required.
 
Option 3 – To reject the Community Safety
Agreement. This option was not required as explained in option
1.
topline: The Head of Law and Governance and Monitoring Officer has decided to endorse the Warwickshire Community Safety Agreement for 2025-2029.

The Bank has not served a

The Council and the Town Trust

Serving the Notice locks the
Bank into a negotiation and a potentially longer lease at a higher
rent, than might otherwise be achieved, though the Court will
assess a rent by reference to the market rent.
