content:
Councillor Cowcher (Deputy Leader – Planning
and Economic Development Portfolio Stratford-on-Avon District
Council)
Councillor King (Place Portfolio Warwick District
Council)
 
The Committee considered a report which
sought Members’ consideration and approval of
revisions to the currently published timetable for preparing the
South Warwickshire Local Plan (SWLP) as contained at Appendix 1 to
the report. The timetable could then inform a revised Local
Development Scheme (LDS) for each District, which would then be
published by each authority. It was a government requirement that
Local Authorities published and kept up to date the Local
Development Schemes (LDSs) for the Local Plan area. The report set
out that the timescale for the publication of the Regulation 19
stage of the SWLP had to be extended from the timetable provided to
Joint Committee in December 2024 to assimilate key evidence being
prepared.
 
The
report set out that, despite this delay in getting the plan to the
Regulation 19 publication stage, it was considered that the SWLP
could be submitted to the Government’s Planning Inspectorate
(PINS) by 31 December 2026 and therefore, be considered through the
existing plan making arrangements. The report set out measures to
be put in place to ensure the document was submission ready and
actions were being taken to mitigate the possibility of further
timetable delays. Nonetheless, the timetable did contain risks
which, if realised, would push the timetable back.
 
The report set out revisions to the
currently published timetable for preparing the SWLP as contained
at Appendix 1to the report and in paragraph 1.3 of the report. The
timetable would inform updated LDSs for both authorities which were
required to be kept up to date by the Government in relation to
Local Plan preparation. The report set out the intention to
commence consultation on the Regulation 19 publication version by
no later than the 8June 2026 so the formal consultation could be
undertaken before the school summer holidays, and to bring the date
forward where the possibility to do so arose. The timetable showed
the intention to submit the plan to the Planning Inspectorate by 31
December 2026 to avoid significant delay in plan preparation by
having to switch to the new plan-making procedures which came into
force after that date for any plans not submitted by
then.
 
The report set out the reasons why the
timetable had to be extended for evidence collection purposes
before the publication version of Regulation 19 consultation could
commence. Primarily the revisions to the timetable were due to
feedback on soft market testing from consultants that could
undertake the studies needed, consultants not being able to
resource a surge in demand from Local Authorities needing support
in preparation of the plan evidence base, a high level of
representations received to the Preferred Options version of the
plan which had needed to be processed, revisions to national
guidance which required the updating of study work done in respect
of the Green Belt, and the need to engage with and gain support
from key consultees to meet the timetable with their own resource
pressures and priorities.  
 
The report set out the risks identified
in achieving the timetable in the report and in Appendices 2 and 3
to the report, and the mitigation being undertaken to address the
risks. This included undertaking due diligence via support from an
experienced Barrister, taking up the offer of support from the
Planning Advisory Service (PAS) to prepare a submission ready plan
by the 31 December 2026, undertaking critical friend review work
with the Planning Inspectorate (PINS) and high-level management
engagement with key consultees providing input on the plan to work
with the timetable proposed at Appendix 1 to the report.
 
The report assessed the alternatives of
the two proposed recommendations contained in the report. That was
to pivot to preparing the plan under the new plan making procedures
and to accept that there would be lengthy delay and associated
higher costs and abortive costs to date; to undertake the
Regulation 19 consultation stage sooner but recognised the
significantly increased risk that the plan might not be supported
by a proportional and sound evidence base; or to stop preparing the
plan with the potential reputational damage, government
intervention, loss of control of a local development strategy for
the area, and the potential for increased speculative development
without planned infrastructure of the scale that could be required
and the potential higher appeal costs associated should the local
authorities choose to refuse the speculative development without a
five-year housing land supply. This analysis helped inform the
recommendations.
 
In
terms of alternative options, the local authorities could look to
pivot preparing the SWLP through the new plan-making arrangements
which were expected to come into force from 1 January 2026, though
secondary legislation was yet to be enacted. However, negatives to
this approach were that it was envisaged that the plan would be
expected to start at stage 1 of the new process. As a result, it
was anticipated that whilst much evidence would have been readied,
there would be an estimated delay of two to three years, based on
informal discussions with the PAS whilst the plan moved through the
new process. This would heighten concerns in respect of time expiry
of the current adopted plans at a time when neither of the Local
Authorities were able to demonstrate delivery of a five-year
housing land supply. In addition, the new system would not be tried
and tested and therefore, there was potential for further delays to
ensue as local authorities and the Planning Inspectorate navigated
the new system. Finally, the delays could result in significant
monies being wasted on the plan to date and it was considered that
costs could increase by pivoting to the new system as delays could
require the evidence to be updated.
 
The
local authorities had looked to see whether they could publish a
Local Plan earlier than proposed and the timetable as set out
reflected this assessment. It was considered that based on feedback
from the consultants undertaking the preparation of studies for the
plan, that if done any earlier the work would not be sufficiently
complete. The timetable was therefore considered to provide the
appropriate balance between doing things quicker and the risk of
failing at Examination. Getting approval for the plan was also key
to moving forward with addressing the five-year land supply issues
now identified within both Districts.
 
If
the Joint Cabinet did not agree a timetable, it was assumed that
officers would nevertheless continue to work on preparing the plan,
but the local authorities would not be in a position to update and
adopt the LDSs for each District. The approach would not be in
accordance with government requirements with unknown consequences
for how the Government might intervene. Nor would it allow the
public, the wider Councillor membership, key bodies, developers,
land promoters, or the Planning Inspectorate (PINS) to be informed
of the likely timescales for plan preparation for the SWLP area and
to manage its resources accordingly to respond when required to do
so.
 
Another alternative option was for the local authorities to stop
preparing a Local Plan for the area. Such an approach would
significantly increase the risk of government intervention and
reduce the ability of the local authorities to be able to manage
development within its own area. The housing requirement set by the
Government would still be required to be met, but proposals would
likely come forward in an unplanned and uncoordinated way based on
speculative applications significantly increasing the risk that a
planned and coordinated approach to the delivery of significant
infrastructure improvements would be lost. Monies spent to date on
the SWLP would also have been wasted whilst costs would be expected
to continue to increase in defending any appeals without a plan
being in place. For reference, Recommendation 2 of the December
2024 Joint Cabinet Committee Report on the SWLP Preferred Options
set out the importance of having an up to date and
‘sound’ Local Plan.
 
The
Warwick District Overview and Scrutiny Committee highlighted the
significant risk that the Local Plan presented to both Warwick
District and Stratford-on-Avon District Council’s. They
requested that officers look at creative ways (including the use of
Artificial Intelligence) to mitigate potential delays to timescales
whilst maintaining quality and placed emphasis on the importance of
‘active travel’. The Warwick District Overview and
Scrutiny Committee encouraged the political leadership of the
Council’s to be active in lobbying government ministers for
flexibility to ensure that this process could be successfully
delivered.
 
The
Stratford-on-Avon District Overview and Scrutiny Committee
requested the following:
 

·          
that changes to the risk register be reported to the
Overview and Scrutiny Committee, along with details regarding
changes in expenditure. Although it was noted that risk was usually
within the remit of the Audit and Standards Committee, it was
thought that the Committee should monitor this in conjunction with
its consideration of other aspects of the SWLP;

·          
that regular updates be provided to the Committee
and the South Warwickshire Plan Advisory Group (SWPAG) to ensure
the timetable was adhered to;

·          
that all information be made available to the public
as soon as possible, and that Ward Members and Town and Parish
Council’s be utilised in the pre-engagement process devised
between officers and the SWPAG;

·          
that significant changes since the previous public
consultation, such as new sites that had since been identified, be
clearly highlighted in the consultation document;

·          
that a communications plan be devised, including
targeted engagement with the areas most likely to be affected by
significant development and offering reasons for changes to the
Plan and opportunities for dialogue;

·          
that additional meetings in 2026 be scheduled as
soon as possible to ensure transparency and members’
availability, and materials provided to the Committee for
consideration at the earliest opportunity; and

·          
that the Terms of Reference and membership details
for the SWPAG be made available to members of the
Committee.
 
The following people addressed the
Joint Cabinet Committee:

 

·          
Councillor
Chilvers, speaking in his capacity as a Ward Councillor for Warwick
District Brunswick Ward; and

·          
Councillor
Rock, speaking in his capacity as Chair of the South Warwickshire
Plan Advisory Group.

 
The Joint Cabinet Committee thanked
officers and Councillors for the significant amount of work
undertaken on delivering the South Warwickshire Local Plan so
far.

 
It was proposed by Councillor
Davison and seconded by Councillor Williams that Recommendation 1
be amended to the following:

 

(1) 
the revised
timetable for the preparation of the South Warwickshire Local Plan
as set out in 1 to the report, be agreed subject to:

 

(a)        
noting with concern that this proposed six-month
delay to the Regulation 19 consultation gravely risks failing to
meet the government’s December deadline;

 

(b)        
bringing forward the timetable for this
consultation if possible; and
 

(c)        
providing councillors with key milestones that
are required to meet this tight timeline and progress reports
against those milestones.

 
It was proposed by Councillor
Williams and seconded by Councillor King that officers
should:

 
·           
set a Terms of Reference with Warwickshire County
Council Transport and Planning, emphasising the Plan requirement to
continue prioritising active and public transport solutions as part
of the 20-minute neighbourhood principles; and
 
·           
plan for further work to as far as possible increase
projected:
 
a)  
built out rates; and
b)  
densities in neighbourhood centres and near
transport hubs.

 
It was proposed by Councillor
Williams and seconded by Councillor King that the Leaders of the
two Councils should speak to the relevant ministers and Civil
Servants as a matter of urgency in respect of the delivery of the
local plan.

 
Councillor King proposed the report
as laid out, subject to the amendments to Recommendation 1 and the
additional recommendations proposed in the meeting, including that
The Joint Cabinet Committee thanked officers and Councillors for
the significant amount of work undertaken on delivering the South
Warwickshire Local Plan so far. It was duly seconded.
 
            
RESOLVED:

 

(1)        
That the revised
timetable for the preparation of the South Warwickshire Local Plan
as set out in Appendix 1 to the report, be agreed, subject
to:

 

(a)        
noting with concern that this proposed six-month
delay to the Regulation 19 consultation gravely risks failing to
meet the Government’s December deadline;

 

(b)        
bringing forward the timetable for this
consultation, if possible; and
 

(c)        
providing Councillors with key milestones that are
required to meet this tight timeline and progress reports against
those milestones;

 

(2)        
That the Local Plan
risk register attached at Appendix 2 to the report and the
Confidential Appendix 3 to the report and the mitigations in
respect of the principal risks as set out in paragraphs 110.1 to
1.10.4 of the report, be noted;

 

(3)        
That officers be
requested to undertake the following actions:

 
(a)     
set a Terms of Reference with Warwickshire County
Council Transport Planning, emphasising the Plan requirement to
continue prioritising active and public transport solutions as part
of the 20-minute neighbourhood principles;

 
(b)     
plan for further work to as far as possible increase
projected a) build out rates and b) densities in neighbourhood
centres and near transport hubs;

 

(4)    
That the Leaders of the two Councils speak to the
relevant ministers and civil servants as a matter of urgency in
respect of the delivery of the Local Plan; and
 

(5)    
That
officers and Councillors, be formally thanked, for the significant
amount of work undertaken on delivering the South Warwickshire
Local Plan so far.
topline: The Joint Cabinet Committee has decided to approve revisions to the timetable for preparing the South Warwickshire Local Plan, despite concerns about potential delays and risks.

purpose:

Mansell Street

decision_maker: Head of Law and Governance and Monitoring Officer
content:
By the Head of Law and Governance: To confirm
appointment of Johnson Controls  to
provide maintenance for SDC’s CCTV systems using a direct
award through the ESPO framework for a three-year period with the
option to extend for a further two years
(https://www.crowncommercial.gov.uk/agreements/RM6289).

The current contract with
Johnson Controls expires on 30 September 2025, and continuing
maintenance and reactive repair of the CCTV system on an ongoing
basis is required now. The direct award will ensure the least
service disruption.
 
This Notice was brought to the
Head of Service’s attention at the end of November and
accordingly was authorised due to the circumstances and the
necessity.


Direct award to
Johnsons Controls under the ESPO framework to continue maintenance
and reactive repair of the CCTV system they are already familiar
with
Carrying out a
further competition through the ESPO framework. There would be some
service disruption during a further competition period as repair
work would not be covered, so this option is considered
unsuitable.
Carrying out a full
open tender process in accordance with SDC’s Contract
Standing Orders. There would be some service disruption during a
full tender process as repair work would not be covered, so this
option is considered unsuitable.
Not appoint a
contractor. This is not a viable option as SDC does not have the
inhouse capacity and technical expertise to carry out maintenance
on the CCTV system, which would degrade without required
maintenance and repair.
topline: The Head of Law and Governance has decided to appoint Johnson Controls for maintenance of SDC's CCTV systems.

content:
Councillor Gist – Law and Governance Portfolio
 
Consideration was given to a
Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) Policy for
Stratford-on-Avon District Council.
 
In receiving the report, it was
noted that an AI Policy would ensure that there was good governance
in respect of its use, and that this was done so effectively and
responsibly. By clearly outlining a set of eight core principles,
to guide the Council’s use of AI, this would ensure that
risks were managed, and data was protected.
 
It was noted that the AI Policy
applied to all Council employees, including temporary staff,
councillors, contractors, consultants, and any third parties or
partner organisations using or sharing the Council’s
information.
 
The options available to The
Cabinet were to adopt the AI Policy, amend the AI Policy and adopt,
or not to adopt the AI Policy.
 
Following which, it
was
 
RECOMMENDED
to Council:
 
That the
Artificial Intelligence Policy at Appendix 1 to the agenda report,
be approved and adopted.
 
Note: This item is not subject to call-in as it is a
recommendation to Council
topline: The Council has decided to approve and adopt an Artificial Intelligence Policy for Stratford-on-Avon District Council.

purpose:
To consider an updated Warmington Parish
Plan.
content:
Councillor Gist – Law and Governance Portfolio
 
Consideration was given to the
adoption of the 2023/2024 Warmington and Arlescote Parish Plan Update which would sit
alongside and complement the previously adopted Warmington and
Arlescote Parish Plan
(2018).
 
In receiving the report, The
Cabinet noted that the Warmington and Arlescote Parish Plan was
considered to be a good example of a parish council working
hard to keep its plan up to date and meeting the needs of
local residents. It was considered that
the update to the Plan would assist in informing the production of
the emerging South Warwickshire Local Plan and associated technical
evidence base documentation, in addition to future planning policy
documents.
 
The options available to The
Cabinet were to adopt the 2023/2024 Warmington and Arlescote Parish Plan Update, suggest amendments
and then adopt the Update, or not to adopt the Update.
 
The Cabinet gave its thanks to
all the volunteers on the work they had undertaken in preparing the
updated plan, in particular the recently retired Chair of the
Parish Council, Mark Burstall,for the dedication and hard work he
had undertaken for the Parish over the last 25 years. 
 
Accordingly, it was
 
         
RESOLVED:                   
 
That
the 2023/2024 Warmington and Arlescote
Parish Plan Update, attached at Appendix 1 to the agenda report, be
adopted as a material consideration when determining planning
applications in accordance with Core Strategy policies, and as an
important source of local information.
 
Note: This item is not subject to call-in to the OSC as it is
not a key decision
topline: The Cabinet has decided to adopt the 2023/2024 Warmington and Arlescote Parish Plan Update.

content:
Councillor Juned – Leader of the Council
 
Consideration was given to
proposals for the installation of electric vehicle (EV) charge
points in Council owned car parks.
 
In receiving the report, it was
noted that Stratford-upon-Avon Town had a high level of tourism,
producing a higher level of demand for public EV charging than
residents or businesses. Increasing the availability of public
charging points would support the local tourism industry by
removing a barrier to visitors staying, especially those using hire
cars where adoption of EVs would be rapid after the 2030 ban on new
car sales. The programme of work would be delivered alongside the
Local Electric Vehicle Infrastructure (LEVI) fund on-street charger
programme which was currently being implemented by Warwickshire
County Council.
 
The Deputy Chief Executive
advised that the EV charge point feasibility study was awaited and
would be presented to The Cabinet upon completion.
 
The options available to The
Cabinet were to support the recommendations, support the
recommendations with amendments to the operating model, support the
recommendations with amendments to the payment model, or not to
support the recommendation.
 
Councillor Crump, Chair of the
Overview and Scrutiny Committee (OSC), provided feedback from the
meeting of the OSC held on 26 November 2025, and noted the
following:
 

·        
Members were advised that the evaluation criteria
for the tender would emerge during the soft market exercise. At the
time, it was unclear what level of interest there was for EV
charging in certain areas. Furthermore, the level of electrical
current available at sites needed to be determined;
 

·        
The potential challenges of finding a commercial
operator to deliver the infrastructure were noted, considering that
town centre charging points were expected to be more commercially
attractive than in rural areas. Suggested options to address this
included reducing rents to make the contact more attractive and
tendering for separate contracts, with a more commercial contract
for the town centre locations and a more social contract for the
rural locations;
 

·        
In response to a suggestion that a single ‘tap
and go’ mobile phone application be used for all sites,
members were advised that this would be the ideal option, but that
being locked into this option could limit the commercial viability.
However, it was noted that having multiple providers and multiple
different applications across the District would be undesirable;
 

·        
Members also discussed home charging, challenges for
urban residents without driveways, grants to install charging
provisions for these residents, and challenges because of planning
restrictions. Members also suggested preferable rates for local
users unable to charge at home; and
 

·        
It was confirmed that security, liability and risk
would be key considerations, particularly in relation to theft of
the materials. Details regarding how undue use of the parking
spaces preventing them being used for charging would be provided
at a later date.
 
Following which, it
was
 
         
RESOLVED:
 
(1)       
That proposals to enable the procurement and
installation of electric vehicle charge points on Council owned car
parks, as detailed in the agenda report, be agreed;
 
(2)       
That procuring a service provider to install and
manage electric vehicle charging infrastructure in Council owned
car parks would be completed through a joint tender process with
Warwick District Council, subject to both Councils’
agreement;

 
(3)       
That approval be given to Officers to explore and
implement the best solution to mitigate any lapse in current
provision, prior to a longer-term solution being procured;
and

 
(4)       
That the Deputy Chief Executive, in consultation
with the Monitoring Officer and S151 Officer, be given delegated
authority to action the proposals set out in the agenda
report.
 
Note: In accordance with the Council’s Constitution, this
item is not subject to call-in to the OSC
topline: The Council has decided to install electric vehicle charge points in Council owned car parks to support local tourism and prepare for the 2030 ban on new car sales.

content:
Councillor Coles – Housing and Customer Services
Portfolio
 
Consideration was given to a
response to a Notice of Motion presented to Council on 14 July
2025, regarding Hospital Access and Information
 
The Motion requested that the
Council worked with key partners in seeking to improve transport
functions. Whilst transportation was predominantly a Warwickshire
County Council function, it was acknowledged that this was a key
issue affecting residents which met a number
of the Council’s Council Plan objectives.
 
The options available to The
Cabinet were to accept the Motion, accept Motion and refer the
matter to Warwickshire County Council as the responsible authority
for transport, or reject the Motion.
 
Following which, it
was
 
RECOMMENDED
to Council:
 
That the
Motion in respect of Hospital Transport and Information be
supported, and in doing so, a summit of key partners be convened to
discuss existing hospital transport arrangements, identify any gaps
and consider potential solutions.
 
Note: This item is not subject to call-in as it is a

content:
Councillor Cowcher - Deputy Leader - Planning and Economic
Development Portfolio
 
Consideration was given to a
response to a Notice of Motion presented to Council on 13 October
2025 which recommended that the proposal put forward by the Motion
be considered as part of the Council’s budget setting process
for 2026/27.
 
The motion called for support
for communities creating and updating Neighbourhood Development
Plans (NDP) by allocating a fund of £250,000 to fill the gap
in funding arising from the end of Ministry of Housing, Communities
and Local Government support for NDP’s and the maintenance of
Localism throughout the District.
 
In receiving the report, The
Cabinet noted that the Notice of Motion sought a budget of
£250,000 which would be sufficient to provide funding of
£8,000 to each of the 29 parishes with current made
neighbourhood plans. This budget could be split across 2-3 years,
thus resulting in additional budgetary pressure of £100,000
in 2026/27.
 
The options available to The
Cabinet were to support the proposal and consider it as part of the
Council’s budget setting process for 2026/27, to allocate
monies to grant fund neighbourhood planning activities of parish
councils by utilising existing Council reserves or not support the
recommendations or the Motion.
 
Following which, it
was
 
         
RECOMMENDED to Council:
 
(1)       
That the proposal be considered as part of the
Council’s budget setting process for 2026/27;
and
 
(2)       
That the Notice of Motion be
supported.

 
 
Note: This item is not subject to call-in to OSC as it is a
recommendation to Council.
topline: The Deputy Leader of Planning and Economic Development has decided to allocate £250,000 to support communities in creating and updating Neighbourhood Development Plans.

content:
Councillor G Cowcher – Deputy Leader – Planning and
Economic Development Portfolio
 
Consideration was given to a
response to a Notice of Motion presented to Council on 13 October
2025 to Support the Re-allocation of some New Housing from
Stratford-on-Avon District to Coventry.
 
The motion called for the
Councils formal support to undertake negotiations with Coventry
City Council regarding allocation of housing numbers in the
Coventry & Warwickshire sub-region with the aim of making best
use of urban and brownfield land, and land in the Green Belt, and
reducing the housing requirement in the South Warwickshire Plan
area.
 
In receiving the report, The
Cabinet noted that the recommendations within the report were based
upon the Council’s duty to co-operate on the development of
strategic policies by virtue of Section 110 of the Localism Act
2011, with the types of strategic matters on which local planning
authorities should cooperate. In order
to be adopted, a Local Plan needs to comply with all the
relevant legislative and procedural requirements, such as the Duty
to co-operate, as well as being sound.
 
The options available to The
Cabinet were not to support the Notice of Motion and continue to
seek to accommodate the additional housing requirement within the
South Warwickshire Local Plan are, or to support the Notice of
Motion and undertake negotiations with Coventry City Council to
seek to accommodate additional housing within its area so as to
reduce the housing requirement in the South Warwickshire Plan
area.
 
In response to a question
regarding Stratford-on-Avon District Council’s 5-year housing
land supply, the Chief Executive clarified that the agenda report
had been compiled specifically to address the original motion and
did not have a broader remit.
 
Councillor Crump, Chair of the
Overview and Scrutiny Committee (OSC), provided feedback from the
meeting of the OSC held on 26 November 2025 and noted the
importance of transparency in ensuring the public understood both
the basis of the District’s
housing allocation and the challenges involved in seeking a
reallocation to Coventry. It was acknowledged that, at present, it
might not be possible for housing from Stratford-on-Avon District
to be reallocated to Coventry. However, other neighbouring local
authority areas that could not meet their own needs could now look
to Coventry before approaching Stratford-on-Avon District Council
to meet their shortfall.
 
In clarification to a further
question, 
the Portfolio Holder confirmed that brownfield sites would
be prioritised first.
 
Following this, it
was
 
        
RECOMMENDED to Council:
 
That, for
the reasons set out in the agenda report, the Notice of Motion
not be supported.
 
Note: This item is not subject to call-in as it is a
recommendation to Council
topline: The Deputy Leader of Planning and Economic Development has decided to not support the re-allocation of housing from Stratford-on-Avon District to Coventry.

content:
Councillor G Cowcher – Deputy Leader – Planning and
Economic Development Portfolio
 
Consideration was given to a
response to a Notice of Motion presented to Council on 13 October
2025 which proposed the Transfer of Public Open Spaces to Private
Owners.
 
In receiving the report, The
Cabinet noted that the provisions of a Section 106 (s106) generally
ran with the land. As such, any change of ownership of land covered
by a s106 agreement had no bearing on the provisions of that
agreement nor the ability of the local planning authority to take
enforcement action for non-compliance, therefore criterion 3 had
already been satisfied. It was further noted that in respect of
criterion 1, 2 and 4, it was proposed that these be added to the
Terms of Reference of the existing Task and Finish
Group.
 
The options available to The
Cabinet were to support the recommendations, not support the
recommendation and seek to deal with matters raised separately, or
not to support the Motion.
 
Following which, it
was
 
        
RECOMMENDED to Council:
 
(1)      
That criterion 1, 2 and 4 of the Notice of Motion
be added to the Terms of Reference of the Transfer of Public Open
Spaces to Private Owners Task and Finish Group, and the group
report back on these issues in early 2026;
 
(2)      
That as detailed in section 1.2 of the agenda
report, criteria 3 confirmed as already satisfied, be noted;
and

 
(3)      
That the Notice of Motion be supported as
detailed in recommendations (1) and (2).
 
Note: This item is not subject to call-in as it is a
recommendation to Council
topline: The Deputy Leader of Planning and Economic Development has decided to approve recommendations regarding the transfer of public open spaces to private owners.

content:
Councillor Juned – Leader of the Council
 
Consideration was given to the
appointment of an external service provider to deliver a Climate
Change Adaptation Audit Programme.
 
In receiving the report, it was
noted that following a pilot phase to gather a sufficient evidence
base, an Action Plan would be produced which would set out how each
organisation could deliver climate resilience
measures.
 
The options available to The
Cabinet were to agree the delivery of a pilot audit programme and
subsequent grant funding, to agree the delivery of the pilot audit
programme but not the subsequent grant funding, or not to increase
climate change adaptation across the District.
 
Councillor Crump, Chair of the
Overview and Scrutiny Committee (OSC), provided feedback from the
OSC meeting held on 26 November 2025 and noted that the majority of the proposed funding would go to
support projects within communities. It was further noted that bids
would be invited from all areas of the District and that the Parish and Town Council
Liaison Officer would promote the grant funding as widely as
possible, including via the Parish Forum.
 
Accordingly, it was
 
         
RESOLVED:
 
(1)  That the
proposals to deliver a pilot Climate Change Adaptation Audit
Programme, as detailed in the agenda report, be supported;
and

 
(2)  That
£150,000 be allocated from the Council’s Climate Change
Reserve to enable the delivery of the Adaptation Audit
Programme.
 
Note: In accordance with the Council’s Constitution, this
item is not subject to call-in to the OSC
topline: The Council has decided to support the delivery of a pilot Climate Change Adaptation Audit Programme and allocate £150,000 from the Climate Change Reserve.

content:
Councillor Juned – Leader of the Council
 
The Cabinet was presented with
the performance achieved during Quarter 2 2025/26, monitoring
delivery of the Council Plan Actions and Key Performance
Indicators.
 
In receiving the report, it was
noted that for the Council Plan Actions due to be reported at the

RESOLVED:
 
That
the position in relation to the Quarter 2 2025/26 Performance

content:
In

Councillor Coles - Housing and Customer Services
Portfolio
 
Consideration was given to
proposals to enable local communities to deliver Local Needs/Local
Choice rural housing schemes with the Rural Housing Enabler (RHE).
The existing Rural Housing Enabler contract with Warwickshire Rural
Community Council ran until March 2026.
 
In receiving the report, it was
noted that The Sustainable Homes, Sustainable Communities Housing
Strategy 2021-2026 required the Council to consider progress
annually and to determine whether the current approach should be
continued. It was further noted that appropriate rural housing was
highly valued by local communities and often emerged as a key
priority within community planning.
 
The options available to The
Cabinet were to endorse the current approach to rural housing
activity, to focus on red communities or to support an alternative
approach to rural housing activity.
 
Councillor Crump, Chair of the
Overview and Scrutiny Committee (OSC), provided feedback from the
meeting of the OSC held on 26 November 2025 and noted the
importance of local involvement, informing local councils of the
role of the Rural Housing Enabler through the Parish Forum and
highlighting the importance of the local housing needs
surveys.
 
Following which, it
was
 
         
RESOLVED:
 
(1)That the
continuation of the existing approach to delivering homes for local
people in rural parishes, as set out in the agenda report, be
endorsed;
 
(2)  That the
existing Rural Housing Enabler contract be renewed for a period of
three years from April 2026 to March 2029, at a cost of
£60,000 per annum; and
 
(3)  That an
exemption to the Council’s Contract Standing Orders be
granted to allow the direct appointment of Warwickshire Rural

content:
To approve the procurement of
contractors to carry out various works at Elizabeth House to comply
with recommendations from statutory regulatory inspections for
health and safety and building maintenance.
 

The works are needed to comply
with health and safety legislation, and extensive due diligence has
been carried out to ensure that the correct scope of works is
carried out, maximising value for money and assisting with
reduction in carbon emissions.
 
Two main areas of work are
required.
1)  
Replacement of emergency lights and various
associated distribution boards and electrical works. Several of the
lights are unable to be repaired due to parts no longer being
available. As they are part of an integrated lighting system this
has meant complete exploration of design options and use of
specialist companies to determine the extent of work needed to
ensure compliance and at the same time maximising opportunities to
reduce CO2 by installing smart scan options.
Due
to this being a recommendation to ensure compliance with
regulations and concerns about staff and public safety in the
building as the nights get darker the work needs to be completed as
soon as possible.
2)  
Repairs and alterations to fire doors and fire
compartmentalisation to meet requirements of Fire Risk Assessments
relative to the current and proposed future use of Elizabeth House.
Comprehensive surveys have been undertaken by specialist companies
to determine the exact scope of the works needed, given the age of
the building, it’s use by staff and members of the public and
to ensure that relevant legislation is complied with.
 
To ensure compliance with the
regulatory reports undertaken for al of these areas, considerable
exploratory work has been undertaken to determine the full extent
of works needed and to agree appropriate solutions. As the areas
are relevant to the occupation of Elizabeth House in a safe and
compliant manner not proceeding with the works is not an option if
the building is to remain open and works need to be carried out as
soon as possible before the onset of winter.

 
·        
To give the Head of Environmental and Neighbourhood
Services approval to proceed with the procurement as
detailed
·        
That the Head of Environmental and Neighbourhood
services provides a progress report to Cabinet within the next 4-6
weeks.
topline: The Head of Environmental and Neighbourhood Services has decided to approve the procurement of contractors for essential works at Elizabeth House.

decision_maker: Head of Housing, Revenues and Customer Services
content:
To award the contract for the
delivery of works relating to Warm Homes: Local Grant for the
period 1 November 2025 – 31 March 2028 to E-ON UK Green
Funding Solutions Limited.  The contract
to be awarded through the Fusion 21 Decarbonisation
Framework.

The new Warm Homes Local Grant
(WHLG) will run from April 2025 for at least three years. WHLG
replaces the previous Home Upgrade Grant (HUG2) scheme, for which
delivery services were provided by E.ON.
 
Under the Department of Energy
Security and Net Zero (DESNZ) guidelines for WHLG, Local
Authorities are permitted to transfer delivery contracts from the
previous HUG2 scheme to the new WHLG. The transfer of delivery
contract was duly carried out and E.ON are currently delivering the
initial stages of WHLG.
 
Council has undertaken a soft
marketing exercise to identify any alternative providers who might
be able to provide equal or superior services to E.ON for the
remainder of the WHLG scheme. After reviewing the services offered
by several potential suppliers, there appeared be no advantage to
changing to an alternative supplier.
 
•             
In addition, there are several advantages to
remaining with E.ON for the remainder of the WHLG
scheme:
•             
E.ON performed extremely well for the HUG2 scheme,
exceeding the delivery targets, and are expected to continue to
deliver the same high standard.
•             
E.ON have supported Stratford-on-Avon District
Council with forecasting and specifications for delivery of the new
scheme.
•             
E.ON have resources available and are able to
complete works in line with funding timescales.
•             
E.ON can provide Stratford-on-Avon District Council
with a full turnkey solution which enables Council to offer a
broader range of upgrades to residents delivered by a range of
subcontractors.
 
The District Council is a
member of the Fusion 21 consortium and can therefore access the
Fusion 21 Decarbonisation Framework for the award of contracts to
fulfil the requirements of the Warm Homes : Local
Grant.  E-ON are registered on this
framework agreement and can be reappointed, as justified above and
in the accompanying Call-off Report.
 
The contract is for the period
1 November 2025 to 31 March 2028 and is of a value of
£1,959,786.15.
 

Stratford District Council is a
small authority with a limited resources allocated to this area of
work (0.6 FTE).  Consequently we require a third
party delivery partner offering wide range of services to
enable us to maintain our track record of high-performance in the
delivery of these carbon reduction and energy efficiency
installations/home improvements. These requirements
include:
 

A strong track record
of delivering installations for Home Upgrade Grant phases 1 and
2.
Wide scope of
available subcontractors to maximise the range of available measure
delivery options.
A large and robust
organisation resulting in resilient and consistent
delivery.
To have an existing
and efficient relationship with Act on Energy, resulting in ease of
workflow processes.
To have an existing
relationship with Warwick District Council which compliments works
planned under other funding streams (particularly
ECO4).
Familiarity with the
WHLG scheme requirements and reporting mechanisms.
Compliance with
accreditation schemes such as Trustmark.
Positive
recommendations from existing partners.
Full turnkey,
flexible service, enabling the District Council to obtain
additional support services as required.

 
E.ON fulfil all
of these requirements. What separates E.ON from other potential service delivery partners
is:
 
•             
Their existing working relationship with our close
partners (Act on Energy and Warwick District Council).
•             
Their national reach in relation to the range of
sub-contractors they are able to call
upon for installation – this will maximise the number of
District residents we are able to assist.
•             
Their flexibility in providing a fully customisable
turnkey solution which Council can adapt as required.
•             
Their strong track record in delivering
installations for the HUG2 scheme in a timely and efficient
manner.
•             
Their good performance under the Warm Homes: Local
Grant scheme work undertaken between April 202 and 31 Oct
2025.
 
An open tender of this work was
also considered however this was ruled out given the resources in
place for this are of work, the time and cost or this type of
procurement exercise and the risks associated with changing the
contracted provider during an existing and ongoing grant
programme.
topline: The Head of Housing, Revenues and Customer Services has decided to award the contract for the delivery of works relating to Warm Homes: Local Grant to E-ON UK Green Funding Solutions Limited.

which would directly address the new Home Office Prevent Guidance
and demonstrate compliance with the Councils Prevent duty in
relation to counter-terrorism.
 
In receiving the report, The
Cabinet noted that Stratford-on-Avon District Council was a
specified authority within the Counter-Terrorism and Security Act 2015, with a
responsibility to have “due regard to the need to prevent
people from being drawn into terrorism” in the exercise of
its functions.
 
The options available to The
Cabinet were to endorse the new Prevent Policy, to amend the
Prevent Policy and endorse, or to request further
information.
 
Councillor Crump, Chair of the
Overview and Scrutiny Committee (OSC), provided feedback from the
meeting of the OSC held on 30 October 2025 and proposed that a
glossary be provided for relevant terms, which was
agreed.
 
Following which, it
was
 
RECOMMENDED
to Council:
 
(1) 
That the new Prevent Policy for Stratford-on-Avon
District Council, to include a glossary of relevant terms, be
adopted; and
 
(2) 
That delegated authority be given to the Head of
Law and Governance and Monitoring Officer to make any minor or
legislative amendments to the Policy should the Law or
Government’s guidance change.

 
Note: This item is not subject to call-in as it is a
recommendation to Council

Consideration was given to
proposals to adopt a Scrutiny Protocol for Stratford-on-Avon
District Council. The Government’s statutory guidance on
overview and scrutiny recommended councils had a protocol in place
to “help define the relationship between the parties and
mitigate any differences of opinion”.
 
In receiving the report, The
Cabinet noted that the adoption of a Scrutiny Protocol would
provide further guidance and clarity regarding the essential remit
of the Overview and Scrutiny Committee.
 
The options available to The
Cabinet were to endorse the Scrutiny Protocol, amend the Scrutiny
Protocol and endorse or not endorse the Scrutiny
Protocol.
 
Councillor Crump, Chair of the
Overview and Scrutiny Committee (OSC), provided feedback
 from the meeting of the OSC held on 30
October 2025 and proposed the following amendment: That the
following sentence be added to paragraph 4.3 of the Scrutiny
Protocol: “The PAPER assessment will be made available to all
members of the OSC after each meeting described in paragraph
4.2.”
 
Following which, it
was
 
RECOMMENDED
to Council:
 
(1)  That the
Scrutiny Protocol be adopted, as amended to include the wording
above; and

 
(2)  That
delegated authority be given to the Monitoring Officer to make any
minor or legislative amendments to the protocol should the
Government’s guidance change.

recommendation to Council

purpose:
IndieGo Plus Demand Responsive
Transport Service in Stratford-on-Avon District
content:
IndieGo Plus Demand Responsive
Transport Service in Stratford-on-Avon District

To extend the current
IndieGo Plus contract with Warwickshire
County Council for a further 12 months subject to continued
performance measures, for the provision of a demand responsive
transport service covering Stratford-on-Avon District.

The IndieGo Plus demand responsive transport service
commissioned and delivered by Warwickshire County Council (WCC)
replaced the UBUS demand responsive transport service in November
2024. UBUS was a jointly commissioned service where WCC
commissioned the third-party vehicle and driver providers and
Stratford-on-Avon District Council (SDC) the booking centre
provider.
 
IndieGo Plus is commissioned by WCC
only with SDC contributing via a contract of £120k per annum
for additional capacity to align the service provision to near what
was previously delivered by UBUS.
 
At SDC’s Cabinet on
6th October 2025 members were presented with an officer
report IndieGo Plus (Formerly
UBUS) Demand Responsive Transport Review of Warwickshire County
Council Provision and Recommendations for Future Services and
subsequently voted to extend the contract with WCC for a further 12
months subject to performance measures being met.
 
The contract with WCC allows
for it to be extended for four further periods of twelve months up
to a maximum time of five years subject to earlier termination in
accordance with the terms.

Several factors have been taken
into account and the following has been
considered in reaching this decision:
 

Whether the budget
allows for these grant awards.
Whether the
organisations are appropriately qualified to undertake this
work.
Whether these
organisations delivered this work effectively with the 2024/25
award.
Whether this work is
aligned with the Growing Opportunities and Council
Plans.
Whether a need exists
for this activity and spending.

 
The answer to all of these questions is
‘yes’.
topline: The Head of Housing, Revenues and Customer Services has decided to extend the IndieGo Plus demand responsive transport service contract in Stratford-on-Avon District for a further 12 months.

content:
Councillor Coles – Housing and Customer Services
Portfolio
 
Consideration was given to the
current operating model at the Fred Winter Centre, including the
emerging financial challenges which placed the future of the Fred
Winter Centre, at risk and the proposed revised operating model,
including revised terms of the Section 106 agreement and grant
funding, to enable Spring Housing Association (Spring) to revise
the operating model to secure this future of the
service.
 
In receiving the report, it was
noted that the whilst the Fred Winter Centre was a core part of the
Stratford-on-Avon District Council’s housing options and
homelessness pathway, the running costs of the scheme far
outweighed the income, and Spring had informed the Council that
this was not viable on a long-term basis. The proposals in the
agenda report provided a solution to enable continuation of the
scheme.
 
The options available to The
Cabinet were to approve the recommendations in full, as set out in
the agenda report, to reject any variation, or request alternate
options be explored.
 
Councillor Crump, Chair of the
Overview and Scrutiny Committee (OSC), provided feedback from the
meeting held on 1 October 2025 and noted a minor amendment in the
OSC report to clarify a support fund.
 
Following which, it
was
 
         
RESOLVED:
 
(1)That the review
of the Fred Winter Centre be noted;
 
(2)  That the new
operating model proposed by Spring Housing Association, to take
effect from April 2026 be endorsed; and
 
(3)  That in respect
of the S106 agreement:
 
a)  
The revisions that may be required to give effect to
the new operating model be noted; and
b)  
That the Head of Development (in accordance with the
existing delegated authority) negotiate and authorise the
completion of a deed of variation to give effect to any such
revisions, subject to:

 
(i)          
The agreement of all those parties with an interest
in the relevant land and their execution of the deed;
(ii)        
Consultation with the Ward Member and Chair of
Planning Committee (as required in the Council’s Scheme of
Delegation)
(iii)       
Consultation with the Head of Housing, Revenues and
Customer Services.

 
Note: In accordance with the Council’s Constitution, this
item is not subject to call-in to the OSC
topline: The Stratford-on-Avon District Council has decided to endorse a new operating model proposed by Spring Housing Association for the Fred Winter Centre to secure its future.

content:
Councillor Cowcher – Deputy Leader – Planning and
Economic Development Portfolio
 
Consideration was given to a
response to a Notice of Motion presented to Council on 8 December
2024, regarding Support for Reinstating the Stratford Southbound
Rail Link.
 
This motion called for the
Councils formal support for the reinstatement of a single track railway line providing a direct
connection from Stratford station to Oxford, Reading, London
(Paddington), Evesham, Worcester, South Wales and the South West. The Motion also called for support for
an additional station at Long Marston Garden Village to serve the
housing developments at Long Marston and Meon Vale.
 
In receiving the report, The
Cabinet noted that the recommendations within the report were based
upon the conclusions of the most recent technical report, that
found that there was merit in continuing to explore the case for
re-opening the line.
 
The options available to The
Cabinet were to support the recommendations, amend one or more of
the recommendations or not support the recommendations or the
Motion.
 
During the debate, questions
were raised and responded to regarding options surrounding light
and heavy rail.
 
Following which, it
was
 
RECOMMENDED
to Council:
 
(1)       
That the three points for noting within the
Notice of Motion to be supported;
 
(2)       
That points 2, 3 and 4 within the Notice of
Motion requesting support be agreed, with point 1 supported in
principle, subject to further work in respect of the South
Warwickshire Local Plan; and

 
(3)       
That points 3 and 4 within the Notice of Motion
requesting resolution be agreed, with point 2 supported in
principle, subject to further work in respect of the South
Warwickshire Local Plan, and point 1 supported in principle,
subject to the findings of any further feasibility
work.
 
Note: This item is not subject to call-in as it is a
recommendation to Council
topline: The Council has decided to support the reinstatement of a railway line connecting Stratford to various destinations and the addition of a new station at Long Marston Garden Village.

content:
Councillor Grocott – Environmental and Neighbourhood
Services Portfolio
 
Consideration was given to a
proposal to revoke (by order) the Air Quality Management Areas in
Studley and Stratford-upon-Avon and approve the production of a
District-wide Air Quality Strategy, following updated guidance
resulting from th introduction to The
Environment Act 2021.
 
In receiving the report, it was
noted that Stratford-on-Avon District Council had declared Air
Quality Management Areas in Studley and Stratford-upon-Avon in 2006
and 2010 respectively following demonstrated non-compliance with
the statutory Air Quality Objective for Nitrogen Dioxide.
Monitoring of both Air Quality Management Areas over three years
had demonstrated a fall that met Air Quality Objective
levels.
 
The options available to The
Cabinet were to approve the revocation of the Air Quality
Management Areas and the production of a District-wide Air Quality
Strategy, or to not approve the revocation of the Air Quality
Management Areas and/or production of a District-wide Air Quality
Strategy.
 
During the discussion of this
item, a request regarding the placement of monitors was raised,
that officers agreed to review.
 
Accordingly, it was
 
         
RESOLVED:
 
(1)        
That the revocation of the Stratford-upon-Avon and
Studley Air Quality Management Areas by Order under the Environment
Act 1995 Part IV, in line with Department of Environment and Rural
Affairs guidance, be approved; and
 
(2)        
That a District-wide Air Quality Strategy be
produced and submitted for future approval.
 
Note: This item is subject to call-in to the OSC
topline: The Council has decided to revoke Air Quality Management Areas in Studley and Stratford-upon-Avon and approve a District-wide Air Quality Strategy.

content:
Councillor Cowcher – Deputy Leader – Planning and
Economic Development Portfolio
 
Consideration was given to
various options that could be pursued to boost the levels of
deliverable housing land supply following the publication of a
planning appeal decision which concluded that Stratford-on-Avon
District Council could no longer demonstrate a 5-year supply of
deliverable housing land in accordance with the National Planning
Policy Framework (NPPF).
 
In receiving the report, The
Cabinet noted that over the second half of 2024 the Government had
made a number of significant changes to
the planning system in England, aimed at supporting its stated
commitment to deliver 1.5 million new homes over the life of the
current parliament. This included an updated version of the
NPPF and a revision of the national
methodology required to calculate the number of homes that local
planning authorities were required to plan for and ensure were
built.
 
It was further noted that there
were a variety of possible measures to enable control of
development across the District,
however, in advance of the adoption of the South Warwickshire Local
Plan, significant increase in planning applications granted
permission would be required.
 
The options available to The
Cabinet were to agree to the preparation of an action plan in order
to address the issues and to seek to demonstrate a 5-year supply
within the quickest possible timetable, identifying any possible
action plan measures where further work is not to be done at this
time, or not agree to the preparation of an action plan.
 
On the agreement of the Chair,
Councillor Rock addressed the meeting and raised concerns regarding
a car park within Southam being identified as a potential housing
sites, which could lead to development in the short to medium term.
These concerns were subsequently addressed by the Head of
Development and the Portfolio Holder for Planning and Economic
Development, who emphasised that car parks were essential to
supporting local infrastructure.
 
Councillor Crump, Chair of the
Overview and Scrutiny Committee (OSC), provided feedback from the
meeting of the OSC held on 1 October 2025 and noted the following
points:
 

·      
That many other councils found themselves in a
similar position and that it had not been unreasonable for the
Council to defend its position of claiming a 5-year housing land
supply based on the Government’s updated method for
calculating housing figures;

·      
That consideration be given on how to support Town
and Parish Councils regarding Neighbourhood Development Plans,
in light of support being withdrawn by
Central Government;

·      
The resource implications of striving to meet the
new target and processing additional planning applications for the
60% of local authorities which found themselves in the same
position;

·      
That the proposed Member Advisory Group regularly
considered progress on the implementation of the action plan and
recommended that the Group could have a role in negotiating with
developers; and

·      
That should the Group be established, the Terms of
Reference and remit be reported to the OSC.
 
Following which, it
was
 
RESOLVED:
 
(1)That the
potential significant implications of being unable to demonstrate a
5-year supply of deliverable housing land be noted;
 
(2)  That any
possible Action Plan measures which The Cabinet do not wish to be
pursued further at this stage, be identified;

 
(3)  That the Head
of Development, in consultation with the Portfolio Holder for
Planning and Economic Development, be delegated to pursue work in
relation to the other possible Action Plan measures;

 
(4)  That a Member
Advisory Group, reporting to The Cabinet, be established by the
Leader of the Council to assist with the delivery and monitoring of
the Action Plan; and

 
(5)  That a further
report on the progress to re-establishing a 5-year housing land
supply be received by The Cabinet by March 2026.
 
Note: In accordance with the Council’s Constitution, this
item is not subject to call-in to the OSC
topline: The Council has decided to address the issue of not being able to demonstrate a 5-year supply of deliverable housing land by approving recommendations for an action plan, delegation of work, establishment of a Member Advisory Group, and a progress report requirement.
